result.summary: The intersection is equipped with standard pedestrian infrastructure including marked crosswalks, curb ramps, and signalization. While sidewalks are present and in good condition, the wide curb radius and lack of physical traffic calming measures may allow for higher vehicle speeds during turns.

hazards.name: Wide curb radius
hazards.description: The corner has a wide radius which allows vehicles to make right turns at higher speeds, increasing risk to pedestrians.

hazards.name: Faded crosswalk markings
hazards.description: The white paint of the crosswalk is showing signs of wear and fading, reducing visibility.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to reduce the crossing distance and slow down turning traffic.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalk with high-visibility ladder or continental markings to improve driver awareness.

result.summary: The image shows a signalized intersection in a mixed-use urban area with sidewalks, curb ramps, and marked crosswalks. While basic pedestrian infrastructure is present, the wide roadway and standard transverse crosswalk markings provide limited protection and visibility compared to more modern safety treatments.

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: The wide curb-to-curb distance increases the time pedestrians are exposed to vehicle traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway at the intersection

hazards.name: Low-visibility crosswalk markings
hazards.description: Standard parallel line markings are less visible to approaching drivers than high-visibility patterns.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve sight lines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Replace existing transverse markings with continental or ladder patterns to increase visibility.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Adjust signal timing to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before vehicles receive a green light.

result.summary: The environment features wide sidewalks and pedestrian signals but lacks marked crosswalks across the main roadway and the large driveway entrance. The presence of multi-story residential buildings suggests high pedestrian demand, yet the infrastructure prioritizes vehicle flow through unmarked conflict zones.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crosswalk
hazards.description: Despite the presence of a pedestrian signal, there are no painted crosswalk markings on the roadway, which may lead to driver confusion and failure to yield.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway in the foreground.

hazards.name: Wide Driveway Conflict Zone
hazards.description: The wide entrance to the parking area lacks clear markings or vertical elements to slow turning vehicles or define pedestrian priority.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-right, where the sidewalk meets the parking lot entrance.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Utility Infrastructure
hazards.description: Large utility poles and associated wiring are positioned near the curb, potentially obscuring sight lines between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image along the sidewalk.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Install zebra or ladder style crosswalk markings to clearly define the pedestrian path and increase driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the crossing distance and improve the visibility of pedestrians waiting to cross.

interventions.title: Driveway Consolidation or Narrowing
interventions.description: Narrow the driveway entrance to reduce vehicle turning speeds and provide a continuous sidewalk level across the entrance.

result.summary: The image shows a signalized intersection with a high-visibility continental crosswalk and a sidewalk on at least one side. While basic infrastructure is present, the environment lacks dedicated pedestrian signals and features to reduce crossing distance or traffic speed.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible at the signalized crossing, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicular signals.

hazards.name: Unprotected Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross two wide lanes of traffic without a median or refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway at the crosswalk

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear right-of-way information.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signage
interventions.description: Add 'Pedestrian Crossing' warning signs (W11-2) to alert approaching drivers of the crossing location.
